name: liquidity_provision_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: By placing limit orders around the running VWAP, we effectively provide liquidity to participants executing VWAP algorithms. Institutional VWAP algos are the single largest source of predictable order flow in Indian equities (estimated 20-30% of institutional volume). These algos target VWAP and will systematically buy below and sell above it throughout the day. By posting bids slightly below VWAP and asks slightly above, we earn the spread while positioning to benefit from VWAP mean reversion. The inefficiency persists because: (1) it requires continuous limit order management which retail traders can't do manually, (2) adverse selection risk from informed traders limits profitability, and (3) capital tied up in open orders reduces return on capital for most participants.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 18; this strategy fails in high-vol (VWAP bands widen, stops hit)
filters.volume_filter: skip if volume_participation < 0.6 (abnormally low volume day)

weaknesses: Limit orders may not fill in fast-moving markets, leading to opportunity cost. In trending days, the strategy may generate zero trades.
Adverse selection: fills are more likely when informed traders push price through the limit level, meaning fills are negatively selected vs random.
Zerodha does not support placing and managing limit orders programmatically with sub-second latency; Kite API has ~200ms round-trip introducing fill risk.
prior_art: Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008) 'High-Frequency Trading in a Limit Order Book' — foundational market-making model. Gueant, Lehalle & Fernandez-Tapia (2012) extend to optimal inventory management. Berkowitz et al. (1988) original VWAP benchmark.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; order book data integration. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
